binding_note: Root-supplied frozen binding consulted; no accepted supplier hashes or validators checked.
scope: Finite connected reduced four-valent sphere diagram, nodes marked crossing or rigid, at least one crossing; kappa counts regions incident to zero distinct crossings and alpha to exactly one distinct crossing. Conclusion kappa+alpha/2-nu<=1. No prime or alternating hypothesis.
actual_read_extent: Entire frozen new draft, including conventions, checkerboard certificates, both induction cases, tables, crossing-free residual and limits.
Actual user primary images proposition6-2-statement-proof-p167-168.png and proposition6-2-proof-end-p168-169.png, including Figure6.4.

independent_checks.finding: PASS: a repeated same-color opposite region gives an exterior simple arc closing through the crossing; conversely the punctured nugatory circle lies in one region. Thus a crossed checkerboard edge is neither loop nor bridge exactly when the crossing is reduced. Rigid loops/bridges remain permitted.

PASS: the connected even-valent sphere shadow admits checkerboard graphs and duals. Regions correspond to primal/dual vertices with distinct marked-edge incidence. Nonloop contraction preserves connectedness; its medial remains connected. The edgeless residual is explicitly the smooth circle.

PASS: disjoint endpoint crossing sets exclude every crossed edge parallel to the contracted rigid edge, hence exclude newly formed crossed loops. Contraction cannot introduce crossed bridges. Only the two endpoint regions merge. All six symmetric table rows follow from w(0)=1,w(1)=1/2,w(n>=2)=0; every beta difference is nonnegative.

PASS: a rigid bridge is safe in the primal, and a rigid loop is safe in the dual. Otherwise the unavailable safe cases yield a crossed parallel edge in each color. The dual two-cycle supplies a two-edge primal bond. Cycle/cut parity forces the two candidate crossings to be the same edge.

PASS: any additional primal parallel edge would form a cycle meeting the two-edge bond once; any additional dual parallel edge would give a cut meeting the established primal two-cycle once. Both are impossible. Therefore each affected region pair shares exactly the one removed crossing, even with other arbitrary rigid and crossed attachments.

PASS: contracting the rigid edge creates no crossed loop except the unique parallel crossing, and no bridge. Deleting that loop introduces no bridge. The operation preserves connectedness/reducedness, removes exactly one rigid and one crossed node, merges exactly the specified black and white pairs, and leaves other incidences unchanged.

PASS: the new crossing count for either pair is r+s-2, because the old crossing sets meet in exactly the deleted crossing. All six symmetric d-table rows are correct; each d>=-1/2, so 1+d_black+d_white>=0.

PASS: with nu=0, a zero/one-crossing region would yield an isolated vertex or crossed loop/bridge in the primal or dual. For connected crossing-free residuals Euler gives beta=2, including the edgeless smooth circle. When the removed crossing was the last crossing, all four old affected regions are one-regions, both d values vanish, and beta(old)=2-1=1. Arbitrarily many remaining rigid nodes cause no additional case.

PASS: if no safe rigid/color choice exists, the exceptional argument applies to any chosen rigid edge. Induction is finite on nu, invoked only when at least one crossing survives. Proof uses finite planar-graph/Jordan-circle and Euler facts, not MT complexity, normal tangles, surface preparation or any accepted flyping normalizer.
